records.mutation: add tabulate-survivors first move and role-swap trap
records.subagent_summary: Fresh run scored 0/8: no rollout ever built the survivor table the hint implies, and all eight instead enumerated factor pairs, declared contradictions, then committed to the same wrong value anyway; two hit the token cap relitigating the same pairs. The dominant confusion was treating uncertainty about which agent holds which number as the ignorance source, so I added one concrete first move (tabulate own-values against surviving partner values) and one explicit trap naming that role-swap is not doubt, keeping the rest of the proven text intact.

records.mutation: make divide-then-take-moduli the explicit first move; replace unused real-root check with a general numeric spot-check
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts scored 1, but one burned ~14.6k completion tokens (vs ~4-5k for the other seven) because it took moduli of the whole equation and raised the constant to the n-th power instead of taking its n-th root - exactly the trap my incumbent named but did not give an operational way to avoid. The seven fast rollouts all divided by (z-b)^n first and got the right ratio immediately, so I promoted that to the explicit first move; separately, no rollout ever used the incumbent's problem-specific 'solve for its real root' verification, so I replaced that dead clause with a shorter, more transferable numeric spot-check against the original equation.

records.mutation: replace weak terminal clause with hard stop rule; add containment trap; drop unused congruence-proof step
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts ended with finish_reason=length at the 16384-token cap and stated no value, despite several repeatedly computing the correct total mid-stream: the failure is pure non-termination plus self-doubt (50-70 'Wait' pivots each), not bad geometry. Two recurring sinks were (a) an incorrect leap that the small square is entirely contained, which reset the whole analysis, and (b) the incumbent's request to confirm angle-independence by pairing congruent pieces, which no rollout completed. I kept the proven coordinate/pruning/shoelace core verbatim, added the one-line containment trap, and swapped the vague 'well before you run long' clause for an explicit trust-the-numbers, never-restart, commit-once-and-stop rule.

records.mutation: pin the per-polynomial cap to deg g = n and name the two off-by-one confusions
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts gave 5/8 with no truncation (all finish_reason stop), so the loss is purely a numeric off-by-one in the per-polynomial cap, not budget or looping. All three failures reached the correct P-L framing the incumbent prescribes but then substituted the wrong root bound: one used the interpolation count (n+1 points determine a degree-n polynomial) and two used the finite-difference degree (n-1), each multiplying that wrong cap by the family size. The edit adds one sentence justifying deg g = n from the untouched leading term and explicitly rules out those two named confusions, leaving the proven framing, traps, and construction clauses intact.

records.mutation: turn the negative-discriminant recovery into an executable move and ban re-deriving confirmed parameters / guessing from magnitudes
records.subagent_summary: 5 of 8 correct; every rollout recovered the curve parameters, so the split came entirely from the direction of the log offset conversion. All three failures produced a negative discriminant and then burned the budget re-verifying parameters they had already back-substituted and confirmed (two hit the 16384-token cap stating nothing) or abandoned the algebra and guessed an area from a side length times a vertical gap. The incumbent diagnosed the inverted offset but prescribed no action, so I made the recovery a concrete one-line swap and added explicit bans on the two observed budget sinks, trimming other wording to stay under the token cap.

records.mutation: add LIFO position-to-timing translation and ban the uniform-position symmetry shortcut, dropping the unfollowed DP clauses
records.subagent_summary: 2 of 8 rollouts scored 1 and none truncated (all finish_reason stop, 9.3k-15.6k completion tokens), so termination and budget were not the failure mode. Five of the six failures abandoned the state graph partway and asserted a hand-wavy 'each bag is equally likely in each position' shortcut yielding 1/n-style values, and several never converted the requested stack position into a statement about which deposit happened when; the incumbent's dynamic-programming and 'probabilities sum to one' clauses were visibly followed by no rollout. I therefore swapped that dead weight for the LIFO position-to-timing translation plus per-step 1/2 path multiplication that both successful rollouts actually used, and an explicit warning against the uniform-position shortcut, leaving the proven opening representation clauses intact.

records.mutation: make the vague index shift an explicit first move; add no-restart/commit rule
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 0/8 with 7 of 8 hitting the token cap: every rollout tried a polynomial/Lagrange framing but none ever performed the incumbent's unnamed 'useful index shift', so the vanishing conditions still started at exponent one and the derivation stalled. They then burned 40-90 self-corrections on hastily mis-stated small cases, concluded the system was inconsistent, and either truncated or committed to an obviously wrong value. The edit keeps the proven functional/Lagrange wording but makes the shift a concrete executable move and adds an explicit do-not-restart-then-commit rule.

records.mutation: generalize problem-specific nouns to a reusable gcd-from-integrality move; add anti-churn rule that markup commutes with division
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts were 8/8 correct with every rollout finishing on stop (2715-6928 tokens), so on-task the incumbent is saturated and the only available gain is transfer, consistent with heldout 0.15 versus train 1.0. Every rollout visibly followed the divide-every-total / gcd / take-maximum clause, so I kept that logic but restated it in unit-agnostic vocabulary instead of the problem's own nouns. Several rollouts wasted 1-3k tokens repeatedly re-asking whether the percentage markup applies before or after dividing, so I added one clause stating that it commutes and to fix an order, replacing the incumbent's vaguer 'apply the stated markup multiplicatively'.

records.mutation: replace unused antisymmetry clause with branch-pruning plus evaluate-through-the-relation
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 4/8; all three zero-reward failures that hit the token cap burned their budget grinding the a=+1 (q = p + constant) branch, and the one non-truncated failure got the first requested value right but slipped a sign while re-expanding q coefficient by coefficient. No rollout ever used the incumbent antisymmetry/fixed-point clause, so I spent those tokens on pruning the impossible branch immediately and on evaluating each target through the affine relation instead of a fresh expansion.

records.mutation: add per-stage bijectivity check, replace piecewise-formula trap with unverified-shortcut trap
records.subagent_summary: 5 of 8 rollouts correct; both zero-reward truncations (finish_reason length at the cap) came from position-by-position bookkeeping that produced non-injective maps (several positions all sent to one slot), after which the student looped and restarted instead of stating anything, and the one early-stopping failure adopted an unverified shortcut claim about the operation's net effect. So I kept the proven first-move/binary-map/commit text and made two surgical swaps: a per-stage 'every label exactly once' bijectivity check that catches exactly the corrupted trace, and a trap clause aimed at unverified shortcut claims (with trace-over-formula precedence) in place of the piecewise-formula clause no rollout followed.
